name: File Drop
tagline: Drop a file onto a form and keep it in the column.

limitations: The Browse button calls context.device.pickFile() first, and the demo sandbox has no device bridge behind its origin, so that call always rejects. What you see instead is the control's fallback — the browser's own file dialog — which is also what a desktop browser does, so the path is real even though the platform call behind it is not.

Dropping a file, browsing for one, the size and type refusals, the image preview and Remove all work for real. Nothing in this control leaves the browser: the file is read with FileReader and written into the bound column, so there is no Web API, navigation or Dataverse call for the sandbox to stand in for.

The empty state’s icon is an resource read with context.resources.getResource, which resolves on a model-driven form and not here. The inline SVG fallback is what the demo shows, and it is drawn to look the same.

presets.name: Nothing yet
presets.description: The empty column, which is the state that invites a drop. Drag a file onto it, or press Browse.

presets.name: An image
presets.description: A picture in the column, shown as a preview. The size beneath it is read back out of the data URL rather than remembered.

presets.name: Not an image
presets.description: A CSV in the same column. There is nothing to preview, so the name and size are the whole of it.

presets.name: Preview switched off
presets.description: The same image with hidePreview set — the property is phrased backwards on purpose, because a TwoOptions input cannot express "unset".

presets.name: Images only, 8 KB
presets.description: A narrow rule and a small limit, so both refusals are reachable: drop a document to see the type refused, drop a large picture to see the size refused.
